test_title: Delhi Police Constable (Executive) 2023 - GK/CA (Held on: 30 Nov, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: Which of the following is the correct statement about the directive principles of state policy?

options.text: Articles 12-35 of the constitution of India deals with directive principles.
Articles 36-51 of the constitution of India deals with directive principles.
Articles 62-71 of the constitution of India deals with directive principles.
Articles 52-62 of the constitution of India deals with directive principles.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Articles 36-51 of the constitution of India deals with directive principles.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enshrined in **Part IV** of the Indian Constitution and span from **Articles 36 to 51.**
 
• They aim to establish a framework for creating a **welfare state** by guiding the government in policy-making and legislation.
 
• The DPSPs are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and are classified into three categories: **Socialistic, Gandhian, and Liberal-Intellectual Principles.**
 
• Although these principles are **non-justiciable** (i.e., they cannot be enforced by courts), they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The provisions include goals such as promoting **economic equality, social justice, environmental protection, and education.**
 
• Examples of DPSPs include **providing free legal aid (Article 39A), securing a uniform civil code (Article 44), and ensuring public health and nutrition (Article 47).**
 
• The state is expected to apply these principles while making laws to achieve the ideals of **justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity** outlined in the Preamble.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Articles 12-35 of the Constitution**__

 __
 
• These articles deal with the **Fundamental Rights** of Indian citizens.
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution and are enforceable by the courts.
 
• They include rights such as **equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, and cultural and educational rights.**
 
• Examples include **Article 14 (Right to Equality), Article 19 (Freedom of Speech and Expression), and Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty).**
 
 
 
• **Articles 62-71 of the Constitution**__
 __
 
• These articles pertain to the **election and terms of the President and Vice-President of India.**
 
• They include provisions for the **election process, qualifications, and conditions of office** for these constitutional positions.
 
• For example, **Article 63 specifies the office of the Vice-President,** while **Article 68** outlines the procedure for filling a vacancy in the office of the President.
 
 
 
• **Articles 52-62 of the Constitution**__
 
 
• These articles focus on the **President of India**, the head of state.
 
• They define the **executive powers, duties, and privileges** of the President.
 
• For instance, **Article 52** establishes the office of the President, while **Article 61** deals with the procedure for impeachment.
